t: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference - Meet in the Middle
o: Split all 2n numbers into two groups of exactly n each and minimize the absolute difference of their sums. Example 1 partitions [3,9,7,3] into [3,9] and [7,3] for a difference of 2, while example 3 manages 0 with [2,4,-9] and [-1,0,-2]. Values may be negative, and n <= 15 means 30 elements: picking which n of 2n go left spans C(30,15) ~ 155 million choices - far too many to evaluate one by one, yet perfectly sized for splitting the search in half.
k: Both sides must have exactly n elements, so subset size must be tracked together with subset sum.
Meet in the middle enumerates the 2^n subset sums of each half separately instead of all 2^(2n) combinations.
Given a left subset of size c with sum a, binary search the size-(n - c) right sum closest to total/2 - a.

a.i: Iterate masks from 0 to 2^(2n) - 1, keep those that select exactly n elements with sum s, and minimize |total - 2s| since the complement automatically forms the other side. Minimal to write, prohibitive to run.
s: Compute the total sum of all elements.
For every mask whose popcount equals n, sum the selected elements into s.
a.t: O(2^(2n) * n) - about a billion masks for n = 15 with inner sums; will not finish.

a.i: Cut nums into left and right halves of n elements and enumerate every subset of each half, recording sums grouped by subset size - 2^n subsets per half. Any valid partition takes c elements from the left and n - c from the right; minimizing |total - 2(a + r)| means finding the right sum r closest to total/2 - a inside the size-(n - c) bucket. Sorting each bucket enables binary search, and the two neighbors of the insertion point suffice to find the closest sum, including under rounding when total is odd.
s: Enumerate masks over n bits, appending the (count, sum) pair of the mask applied to the left half and to the right half.
Sort every right-half bucket by sum.
For each left entry (c, a), binary-search total/2 - a in bucket n - c.
Score the neighbors at indices j - 1 and j, updating min |total - 2(a + r)|.
a.t: O(2^n * n) - subset enumeration dominates; sorting adds 2^n log 2^n and matching is 2^n binary searches.
a.sp: O(2^n) - subset-sum buckets for both halves.

w: Grouping by subset size is the make-or-break detail - skipping it mixes partitions with unequal halves and produces wrong answers. Negative values are precisely why the classic subset-sum DP on total does not apply and meet-in-the-middle does. Keep intermediates in 64-bit (sums reach +-3 * 10^8 and are doubled during scoring). To extend the solution, store the generating mask next to each sum to reconstruct an actual partition; a common follow-up asks exactly that.
